evals.name: publish-handoff-under-limit
evals.prompt: I'm about to hit my usage cap on this account and I don't want to lose everything we've worked out here. I run a separate claude-work profile on this machine — get this conversation over to it so I can keep going there.
evals.expected_output: Nonce echoed in its own Bash call, publish_session.py run in a later call, transcript copied into the shared dir, session id + the consume command reported back.
assertions: Echoed a nonce in an earlier, separate Bash call and reused it verbatim
Used publish_session.py instead of hand-copying a transcript
Exactly one transcript landed in the shared dir, parses, and is the id reported to the user
Reply gives the session id AND the consume-session command to run
Reply flags the snapshot boundary or the privacy of a full transcript

evals.name: consume-digest-and-summarise
evals.prompt: My personal account published session 7c2f19a4-3b8e-4d51-9a02-6f4e1c88b3d7 over to me. Pull it in and tell me where they actually got to, then clean up after yourself.
evals.expected_output: Digest produced via the script (not a raw read of the 0.5 MB jsonl), summary naming the double-counting root cause and the unfinished work, then a keep-or-delete question.
assertions: Used consume_session.py rather than parsing the transcript by hand
Produced a digest of the shared session
Did not dump the raw 0.5 MB transcript into context
Whole run cost under 120k tokens
Summary names the real root cause (portions double-counted per school and per menu)
Summary carries forward the unfinished work (root Dockerfile / missing index)
Asked the user whether to keep or delete the staged copy
